reference: ANSI/ANS-5.1-1979 fission-product decay-heat shape functions (23-term fits for thermal U-235, thermal Pu-239 and fast U-238); a generalised Bateman solution for branching decay chains implemented independently in 50-digit arithmetic and crosschecked against scipy.linalg.expm; the IAEA Nuclear Data Section evaluation of spontaneous-fission neutron yields; and ENSDF half-lives, Q values, branching ratios and mean decay energies retrieved from the IAEA Live Chart API.  Fission-product decay heat is carried against a SECOND, independent reference as well: direct summation over the ENDF/B-VIII.0 neutron-induced fission-yield sublibrary (England and Rider, ENDF-349) and the ENDF/B-VIII.0 decay sublibrary, the whole decay network solved from the independent yields.  Grading stays against ANS-5.1; the summation is recorded per case as the crosscheck, and the two references agree to better than 5 % on every one of the 65 decay-heat cases (worst ENDF/ANS = 0.9505 at 30 s after fast fission of U-238), so no case is excused on the grounds that the references disagree.  The Way-Wigner correlation is carried as an order-of-magnitude crosscheck only and is never graded.
reference_citations: ANSI/ANS-5.1-1979, Decay Heat Power in Light Water Reactors, Tables 1-3 (23-term fission-product shape functions for thermal U-235, thermal Pu-239, fast U-238); coefficients transcribed from Westinghouse WCAP-16009-NP-A Tables 8-1, NRC ADAMS ML050910161.
K. Way and E. P. Wigner, 'The Rate of Decay of Fission Products', Phys. Rev. 73 (1948) 1318.

S. Simakov, M. Verpelli, N. Otsuka, 'Update of the nuclear data for the neutron emissions for actinides of interest in safeguards', IAEA Nuclear Data Section, 2015-03-13, Table 1 (SF neutron yields, n/s/g).
IAEA Live Chart of Nuclides / ENSDF, relnsd API (https://nds.iaea.org/relnsd/v1/data), retrieved 2026-08-11.
H. Bateman, 'The solution of a system of differential equations occurring in the theory of radioactive transformations', Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 15 (1910) 423.

ENDF/B-VIII.0 neutron-induced fission-product yield sublibrary (England & Rider, ENDF-349) and radioactive decay sublibrary (MF=8 MT=457), retrieved from the IAEA Nuclear Data Section mirror https://www-nds.iaea.org/public/download-endf/ENDF-B-VIII.0/ on 2026-08-12; decay heat by direct summation over the full decay network started from the independent yields.
tolerance: 5 % relative on fission-product decay heat against ANSI/ANS-5.1-1979.  That is one combined standard deviation: the standard is itself a fit whose evaluated uncertainty on f(t,T) is a few per cent, and the second independent reference used here - an ENDF/B-VIII.0 summation - itself sits 0 to 5 % below ANS-5.1 across these cases.  It is not chosen from the tool: it is the mutual spread of the two references, and two cases still fail it.  1e-6 relative on the decay solver against the closed-form Bateman solution, because that is exact mathematics and the two independent reference implementations agree to 3e-11.  1e-12 relative on the source-term identities, which are exact arithmetic within one call.  1 % on half-lives and 3 % on energy deposited per decay against ENSDF, which is the level at which an engineering decay library is normally rounded.  On spontaneous-fission neutron yields, the larger of 5 % and the 1 sigma the IAEA table quotes for that nuclide.
independence_note: Every decay-heat case is now a blind test.  Until 2026-08-12 the tool calibrated its lumped short-lived fission-product groups on the Way-Wigner / ANS-5.1 law for thermal U-235, which made the U-235 cases a test of faithful implementation rather than of prediction.  Those group yields are now derived, per fissioning nuclide, from the ENDF/B-VIII.0 fission-yield and decay sublibraries with no reference to ANS-5.1 (see the derivation in /root/bench/ref/fy/derive_final.py), so the U-235 cases are as independent of the reference as the Pu-239 and U-238 ones.  The Bateman, ENSDF, SF-yield and identity cases were always independent.

not_benchmarked.gamma_dose_rate: The dose panel (Sv/h at a distance) uses a single-energy point-kernel with a lumped self-absorption thickness and no build-up factor.  There is no published verification case that matches that geometry closely enough to grade it, and the tool itself calls the model coarse, so it is left untested here rather than graded against a shielding calculation it does not claim to be.
not_benchmarked.alpha_n_yields: (alpha,n) production is a single power law in the alpha energy times a matrix factor. Evaluated thick-target yields exist per matrix (Perry & Wilson, LA-8869-MS) but the tool does not expose the per-matrix yield, only the summed neutron source, and in oxide fuel the (alpha,n) share is a few per cent, so the SF cases dominate any comparison.  Not graded.
not_benchmarked.activation_products: The structural-activation part of the inventory (Co-60, Ni-63, Nb-94 ...) depends on trace impurity levels the user enters; there is no reference inventory to compare against without adopting the tool's own impurity assumptions.
not_benchmarked.fission_product_yields: The per-nuclide chain yields of the ~150 explicitly tracked fission products are not graded against ENDF/JEFF one by one here; only their aggregate effect through the decay-heat comparison is.  (A spot comparison against ENDF/B-VIII.0 cumulative yields finds them within 15 % for all but a handful of low-yield nuclides, plus the deliberate exceptions where the tool assigns the chain yield to an upstream member such as I-135 -> Xe-135.)  The yields of the twelve lumped short-lived groups ARE derived from ENDF/B-VIII.0 and their derivation is checked here through the decay-heat cases.
